decision_triggers: If line_loss_events stays at 1 or more on the S-bend or slalom with this geometry, the cause is still not geometric. Keep geometry fixed and report where on the course the loss begins.
If line_loss_events is 0 on all three tracks but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, the next geometry step is wheel_track 0.12 m for more differential turn authority.
If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed.
integration_questions: At what course position do the S-bend and slalom line losses begin, and what are the sensor readings and the steering signal at that moment?
Does last_direction or a search direction change the S-bend and slalom loss count with geometry held fixed?
Do the outer sensors at ±0.05 m read near zero on most of the course, and is the controller still steering correctly from the centre sensors?

intent: Hold the iteration 7 geometry unchanged, so that any change in S-bend and slalom line loss comes from the controller or start pose and not from the body. Geometry edits stay queued: wheel_track 0.12 m only if line loss is zero on all three tracks and max_error still nears 0.06 m; wheel_radius 0.035 m only if runs complete and completion_time exceeds 2.5 s. Expected result: the score stays near 54 unless the Integrator clears the S-bend and slalom losses. If they clear, progress on those tracks should rise sharply and max_error becomes the next geometry test.
learning: Iterations 3 to 7 show that the ±0.05 m span removes oval line loss, that mass has negligible effect, and that S-bend and slalom loss persists with every geometry that clears the oval. Iteration 8 holds geometry to test whether the controller-side or start-pose change clears those losses. If it does not, the next geometry test is wheel_track 0.12 m, the only geometry lever left for bend overshoot.
rationale: Iteration 7 raced the iteration 5 geometry (seven 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 × 0.12 m) and scored 53.68. The oval logged 0 line-loss events, but the S-bend and slalom each logged 1, with max_error about 0.060 to 0.064 m and progress 0.16 and 0.11. Across iterations 3 to 7 the ±0.05 m span cleared the oval loss, while mass (0.7 to 0.6 kg) changed max_error by under 0.002 m and progress by about 0.01. Body width cannot move the 0.06 m off-track limit. The detection geometry predicts that the outer sensors see tape to about 0.07 m offset, which is beyond the off-track limit, so a plain sensor-coverage failure is unlikely. The Integrator's rule says that if S-bend and slalom line loss stays at 1 with geometry fixed, the loss is not geometric and geometry should not be edited. Both the Integrator's feedback and the evidence support that. The wheel_track 0.12 m step is only triggered when line loss is zero on all three tracks, which is not the case. The wheel_radius step is only triggered when runs complete, which they have not. I therefore hold the geometry exactly as in iterations 5 and 7. Changing geometry now would also invalidate the controller work the Integrator is doing, and would confound the test of whether controller-side line-loss handling or start pose clears the losses.
